# healthcheck

```go
import "gorontalo/pkg/httpkit/healthcheck"
```

Package healthcheck registers a small set of common HTTP endpoints on a standard library \*http.ServeMux. It has no third\-party dependencies.

It exposes three probes, each on its own path so orchestrators such as Kubernetes can target them independently:

- a health check \(GET /healthcheck\) that confirms the process is up,
- a liveness probe \(GET /livez\) that fails when the process is unrecoverable and should be restarted,
- a readiness probe \(GET /readyz\) that fails when the process is up but not yet able to serve traffic, so it is pulled from rotation.

Liveness and readiness run any checks registered for them and report ready only when every check passes. A failing probe returns 503 with a JSON body naming the failed checks; a passing probe returns 200.

### Usage

```
h := healthcheck.New(healthcheck.Config{
    ReadinessChecks: map[string]healthcheck.Check{
        "db": func(ctx context.Context) error {
            return db.PingContext(ctx)
        },
    },
})
mux := http.NewServeMux()
h.Register(mux)
http.ListenAndServe(":8080", mux)
```

Register may target any \*http.ServeMux, so these endpoints can share a mux with an application's own routes.

<a name="Check"></a>
## type [Check](<https://github.com/xwinata/goliath/blob/main/pkg/httpkit/healthcheck/options.go#L8>)

Check reports whether a dependency is healthy. It returns nil when the dependency is ready and a non\-nil error describing the problem otherwise. The context carries the request deadline, so a Check should respect cancellation.

```go
type Check func(ctx context.Context) error
```

<a name="Config"></a>
## type [Config](<https://github.com/xwinata/goliath/blob/main/pkg/httpkit/healthcheck/options.go#L13-L35>)

Config customizes a Handler created by New. The zero value is valid: empty paths fall back to their package defaults, and nil check maps mean the corresponding probe simply confirms the process is up.

```go
type Config struct {
    // HealthPath is the path served for the simple health check. Empty selects
    // defaultHealthPath.
    HealthPath string

    // ReadinessPath is the path served for the readiness probe. Empty selects
    // defaultReadinessPath.
    ReadinessPath string

    // LivenessPath is the path served for the liveness probe. Empty selects
    // defaultLivenessPath.
    LivenessPath string

    // ReadinessChecks are the named checks run by the readiness probe, which
    // reports ready only when every check returns nil. Entries with an empty
    // name or nil Check are ignored.
    ReadinessChecks map[string]Check

    // LivenessChecks are the named checks run by the liveness probe, which
    // reports alive only when every check returns nil. Entries with an empty
    // name or nil Check are ignored.
    LivenessChecks map[string]Check
}
```

## type [Handler](<https://github.com/xwinata/goliath/blob/main/pkg/httpkit/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L115-L121>)

Handler serves the health, liveness, and readiness endpoints. Create one with New and wire it into a mux with Register.

```go
type Handler struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="New"></a>
### func [New](<https://github.com/xwinata/goliath/blob/main/pkg/httpkit/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L126>)

```go
func New(cfg Config) *Handler
```

New creates a Handler configured by cfg. A zero\-value Config serves the default paths with no readiness or liveness checks \(so both probes simply confirm the process is up\).

<a name="Handler.Register"></a>
### func \(\*Handler\) [Register](<https://github.com/xwinata/goliath/blob/main/pkg/httpkit/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L140>)

```go
func (h *Handler) Register(mux *http.ServeMux)
```

Register mounts the Handler's endpoints on mux. It registers the health, liveness, and readiness paths, each restricted to GET.

<a name="Status"></a>
## type [Status](<https://github.com/xwinata/goliath/blob/main/pkg/httpkit/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L56>)

Status is the condition reported in a probe response body. Its zero value is StatusOK.

```go
type Status int
```

<a name="StatusOK"></a>

```go
const (
    // StatusOK is reported when a probe passes.
    StatusOK Status = iota
    // StatusUnavailable is reported when a probe fails.
    StatusUnavailable
)
```

<a name="Status.MarshalJSON"></a>
### func \(Status\) [MarshalJSON](<https://github.com/xwinata/goliath/blob/main/pkg/httpkit/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L80>)

```go
func (s Status) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error)
```

MarshalJSON encodes the Status as its String label so probe response bodies stay stable \(e.g. \{"status":"ok"\}\) regardless of the underlying int values.

<a name="Status.String"></a>
### func \(Status\) [String](<https://github.com/xwinata/goliath/blob/main/pkg/httpkit/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L67>)

```go
func (s Status) String() string
```

String returns the lowercase label for s, e.g. "ok" or "unavailable". Unknown values render as "unknown".

<a name="Status.UnmarshalJSON"></a>
### func \(\*Status\) [UnmarshalJSON](<https://github.com/xwinata/goliath/blob/main/pkg/httpkit/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L86>)

```go
func (s *Status) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error
```

UnmarshalJSON decodes a Status from its String label. An unrecognized label is an error so malformed input is not silently accepted.
